tasks.short: Commission pre-building cost and energy assessments.

steps.what: Prepare a rough order of magnitude cost range.
Contract others for a feasibility assessment if needed.
Sign the brief for the energy or environmental assessment.

tasks.design: Early quantities produce a rough order of magnitude cost range in {ERP}. The construction manager decides whether that range is enough or whether to contract others for a feasibility, energy-efficiency, environmental, or sustainability assessment, and signs the brief. The range does not declare the project feasible. An empty quantity stops the range.
tasks.previous_blocker: The first number in the room became the budget, with no range and no decision to buy a real study.
tasks.enabler_now: Early quantities can show a range. Feasibility is still a judgement, and a specialist study is still a contract.
tasks.still_hard: Quantities that are only a sketch, and an environmental question a cost range cannot see.
tasks.human_edge: The manager knows when the range is too wide to take to a client, and which question a consultant must answer.
tasks.altitude: A range exists before the conversation. The manager still decides what to contract and still signs the brief. The range is not a feasibility finding.

reach.task: Ask for an assessment when the desk figure cannot answer the environmental question.
reach.learn: A cost range is not that assessment. This manager still signs the brief.

evidence.claim: Early quantities can produce a cost range. They cannot perform an energy or environmental assessment.
Commissioning an assessor spends money and sets a scope. The manager signs the brief. The job digest treats bids and professional judgement as a person's decision.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: A construction manager at a European contractor or client team. National building rules apply. A register does not replace a site visit.

Fields: Quantity id and a unit rate band, produced by the early takeoff. A missing quantity is excluded from the range and named as excluded. If a required field is missing, the step stops and the manager finishes it by hand.
Native check: Use the existing cost codes before a new estimating product.
Any edit after approval voids the version and returns the item to the manager.
unknowns: Who may commission an external assessor.
Which assessments the client already holds.
research_questions: How wide is the rate band at this stage?
Which assessments are required before planning consent?

already_counted.description: The manager still decides which assessment to contract.
The manager still signs the brief.

incremental.description: The manager updates the rate band when the company changes its early-stage rates.

approvals.approved_version: brief id and the scope text shown to the manager

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The decision to contract a study stays with the manager. Saving is the rough range, and it shrinks when quantities are too thin for a rate to mean anything.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Evaluate methods with the cost model.

steps.what: Run the computer model on these construction methods.
Evaluate construction methods for cost effectiveness.
Record which method the plan will use.

tasks.design: A cost model, which is a calculation on rates and quantities and not a drawing checker, runs in the {ERP} cost tables for the methods the manager named. The construction manager evaluates cost effectiveness and records the method the plan will use. The model does not choose. A method with no rate is shown as not calculated.
tasks.previous_blocker: One method was priced properly and the other was a guess, so the comparison was theatre.
tasks.enabler_now: Named methods with rates can be calculated on the same basis. The choice is still the manager's.
tasks.still_hard: A method the rate library has never seen, and a saving that depends on a crew the model does not know.
tasks.human_edge: The manager can reject a cheaper method that this site cannot build safely.
tasks.altitude: Both methods get a number from the same rates. The manager still evaluates them and still records the choice.

reach.task: Compare options on one set of rates, then choose.
reach.learn: The model output is not the decision. This manager still evaluates the method.

evidence.claim: Rates and quantities can be calculated for methods that are already named. The calculation does not invent a method.
Choosing how to build can affect safety. The manager chooses. Nothing in this step checks a drawing for code, and no product from a drafting digest is used.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: A construction manager at a European contractor or client team. National building rules apply. A register does not replace a site visit.

Fields: Method id and rate id, produced by the manager's list and the rate library. A method without a rate is not given a fabricated cost. If a required field is missing, the step stops and the manager finishes it by hand.
Native check: Run the comparison in the existing cost tables. The other system is that cost model, named in the step.
Any edit after approval voids the version and returns the item to the manager.
unknowns: Which methods are allowed on this project.
Whether the rate library matches local labour cost.
research_questions: Do the methods being compared share a rate library?
How often is the cheapest method rejected?

already_counted.description: The manager still evaluates the methods.
The manager still records the choice.

incremental.description: The manager adds a rate when a method is new to the library.

approvals.approved_version: method ids and the model figures shown to the manager

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The evaluation stays with the manager, so saving stays under half. It shrinks further when a method has no rate and cannot be calculated.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Inspect the site for environmental rules.

steps.what: List the environmental rules named for this site.
Inspect the project against those environmental regulations.
Write the environmental finding from the visit.

tasks.design: Environmental rules already attached to the site are listed from {DOCS}. The construction manager inspects the project against them on the ground and writes the finding. The list does not monitor compliance. A rule that needs a sample or a laboratory is not closed on this visit.
tasks.previous_blocker: The environmental pages stayed in the consent folder, and the walk looked for whatever the manager remembered.
tasks.enabler_now: Named rules can be listed. The ground still has to be seen.
tasks.still_hard: Seasonal constraints, neighbours, and a condition that needs a measurement the manager cannot make.
tasks.human_edge: The manager can see silt in the water and a barrier that has been moved, which the consent text does not update.
tasks.altitude: The visit starts from the site's own rules. The inspection stays with the manager. A desk review does not replace it.

reach.role: Brownfield Redevelopment Specialists and Site Managers
reach.task: Walk the site before accepting a desk statement about the ground.
reach.learn: A rule list is not the inspection. This manager still goes.

evidence.claim: A consent can be listed as rules. It cannot observe the site.
An environmental finding can affect whether work may continue. The manager writes it from the visit. No automated judgement of harm is made.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: A construction manager at a European contractor or client team. National building rules apply. A register does not replace a site visit.

Fields: Site id and rule id, produced by the planning or permit conditions stored for the project. A condition that is not stored is not shown, and the manager does not treat silence as compliance. If a required field is missing, the step stops and the manager finishes it by hand.
Native check: Read the conditions already filed on the project.
unknowns: Which conditions are environmental rather than planning design.
research_questions: Are permit conditions stored as separate rules?
Which conditions need a laboratory rather than a look?

already_counted.description: The manager still inspects the site.
The manager still writes the finding.

incremental.description: The manager adds a rule when a new condition is issued.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The inspection is the task. Saving is the list of rules already on file, and it disappears when the conditions were never split out of the consent PDF.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Open protection measures used on a similar site.
Implement the program by signing it for the site.

tasks.design: Measures used on a similar site are opened from {DOCS}. The construction manager develops the environmental protection program for this site and signs the version to implement. The library does not adopt a measure. A measure that does not match a rule on this site is dropped until the manager writes why it is still needed.
tasks.previous_blocker: The last site's silt plan was copied and did not match this watercourse.
tasks.enabler_now: Past measures can be opened. This site's program is still written and signed by the manager.
tasks.still_hard: A habitat constraint, a neighbour, and a measure the crew will not maintain.
tasks.human_edge: The manager knows which measure will be kept in place on a wet Friday and which one exists only in the plan.
tasks.altitude: The draft starts from real past measures. The manager still develops this site's program and still signs it.

reach.task: Set a protection measure that operations will actually run.
reach.learn: A library is not the program. This manager still signs what the site will do.

evidence.claim: A library can store past measures. It cannot tell which measure this watercourse needs.
Implementing a protection program is the manager's decision. The job digest says an owner decides on obligations. No automated finding of environmental harm is produced.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: A construction manager at a European contractor or client team. National building rules apply. A register does not replace a site visit.

Fields: Site type and measure id, produced by the library. Each adopted measure must cite a site rule id or a reason the manager writes. If a required field is missing, the step stops and the manager finishes it by hand.
Native check: Use the existing environment folder before a new system.
Any edit after approval voids the version and returns the item to the manager.
unknowns: Which measures the consent already requires.
Who trains the crew on the signed program.
research_questions: Are past measures written so another site can read them?
Which measures failed on the last project?

already_counted.description: The manager still develops the program.

incremental.description: The manager retires a measure that this site's consent does not support.

approvals.approved_version: program version and the measure list shown to the manager

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Writing and signing the program stay with the manager. Saving is opening similar measures, and it shrinks when no past site is actually similar.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The manager still judges a feasibility study, still walks the site for environmental rules, and still writes the protection program. A cost range can be calculated first.
reach: Chief sustainability officers compare an option's environmental load with its cost, and the site judgement stays here.
Brownfield redevelopment specialists walk the ground before they trust a desk study.
skills_to_grow: Treat a cost range as a range, and commission a person when the range is not a decision.
Keep an environmental finding tied to what was seen on the site.
role.ambitious_version: A rough cost range is ready before the feasibility conversation, and the manager still decides which study to buy.
